1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with clear line spacing and well-separated elements, though letter spacing appears to be standard default rather than specially increased.

2.why: No italics or dense text blocks appear anywhere and instructions are in sentence case; the only all-caps text is the 'YOUR ONLINE BANK' brand header rather than instructional content.

3.why: Screenshots are desktop-width, but all content sits in a narrow single-column card (~590px) with large text and buttons that would reflow cleanly to a mobile viewport.

4.why: Every instruction is a single short plain-language phrase, e.g. 'Set up an extra check for protected payments.' and 'Multi-factor authentication is active.'

5.why: No input field shows a placeholder, format hint, or worked example; the values visible in step 9 (marcus@example.com, +441234567890) are persisted user entries after an error, not examples.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is one sentence; the only lengthy text is in the demo 'Logs' panel, which is clearly marked as a simulation aid and not required reading.

7.why: The manual secret and recovery codes are rendered as selectable page text so copy-paste is technically possible, but no copy button, select-all, or download affordance is provided.

8.why: Step 4 offers only a typed 'Manual secret' string for authenticator setup with no QR code, provisioning link, or any equivalent alternative visible.

9.why: The email and mobile fields are standard labelled inputs with no visible blocking of autofill, but no autocomplete attributes or password-manager behaviour can be confirmed from static screenshots (and there is no password field at all).

10.why: Every screen has a large bold heading naming the current step ('Sign in', 'Verify your identity', 'Set up authenticator', 'Save recovery codes', 'MFA settings') and a single prominent blue primary button.

11.why: Each step centres on one task, but steps 4 and 6 leave the 'Create secure setup code' / 'Generate recovery codes' buttons visible alongside 'Confirm authenticator' / 'I have stored these codes', so two same-styled actions coexist at those moments.

12.why: Only the final screen plainly states an outcome ('Multi-factor authentication is active.'); intermediate transitions (e.g. after identity verification) give no confirmation of what happened, the next step is only implied by the new heading.

13.why: The error state explicitly invites retry ('Please try again') with entered values retained and no lockout or penalty shown, and the generate/create buttons remain available implying re-request, though no reveal/hide toggle for secrets exists.

14.why: The only error shown, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming and gives an action, but it does not state what the actual problem was.

15.why: No countdown, timer, or session-expiry warning appears on any screen, so no reading or entry time limit is observed, though the actual allowed time window for codes cannot be verified from screenshots.
